facts: In this appeal by special leave, the common judgment of the Punjab and Haryana High Court dated 22 December 2006 in Murder Reference No.12 of 2005 and Criminal Appeal No.10-DB of 2006, affirming the conviction and sentence of death imposed on the appellant by the Sessions Judge, Sangrur by judgment dated 7 December 2005 in Sessions Case No.25 of 2003 is under challenge.
The appellant Des Raj is a retired police constable. Chand Singh, the complainant is a distant relative of Des Raj. Des Raj and Chand Singh with their respective families reside in adjoining houses.
On 16 February 2003, both families attended the Bhog ceremony in connection with the Birth Anniversary of Baba Ravi Dass and returned home in the afternoon.
Des Raj was fully drunk when he returned home.
issues: Whether the courts below were justified in imposing the sentence of death?
petitioner_arguments: The challenge is restricted only to the imposition of capital punishment. The appellant drew our attention to the various mitigating circumstances and contended that this is not a rarest of rare case, requiring death sentence.
respondent_arguments: The learned counsel for the State countered by relying upon the aggravating circumstances listed by the High Court.
court_reasoning: In Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab [1980 (2) SCC 684 1980 Indlaw SC 586] and Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab [1983 (3) SCC 470 1983 Indlaw SC 116], this Court has stated the principles and guidelines relating to award of death sentence.
The High Court held that on balancing the mitigating circumstance and the following aggravating circumstances, the scales tilted in favour of death sentence :
In a sense, to kill is to be cruel and therefore all murders are cruel. But such cruelty may vary in its degree of culpability.
holding: The High Court affirmed the judgment of the trial court, and confirmed the death sentence awarded to Des Raj.
